title: spec review: S2a1 memory_hot: bounded HOT memory view generated from the store, never-compact classes, deterministic compaction, memory hot/compact CLI (P1 HOT, P4)
spec:
Create orchestrator/memory_hot.py on top of memory_store (S1a). Config in pool.toml [memory]: hot_budget_tokens = 3000 (dated comment; tokens estimated as chars/4 like skills_registry._token_estimate), hot_never_compact = ["gotcha:unresolved", "architecture", "decision:constraint"], hot_recent_days = 14. build(root, budget_tokens=None) -> {"records": [...], "tokens": n, "dropped": [ids], "pinned": [ids]}: candidates = all warm records; pinned (never compacted) = architecture records, gotchas whose outcome is empty or says unresolved/open, decisions tagged constraint or security, and any record whose source_task is a task that is not merged/done/failed on the bus; the rest ranked by score = recency (days since date, decaying over hot_recent_days) + kind weight (gotcha 3, decision 2, architecture 2, model_note 1, retrospective 1, strategy 1, skill_outcome 1) + 1 per open bus task whose title or scope mentions one of the record's components; fill the budget by score after the pinned set; if the pinned set alone exceeds the budget, keep it and report over_budget = true (never drop pinned). Each record is rendered as one compact line (date, kind, title, and for gotchas the first sentence of the body) plus a pointer line 'memory show <id>' only for governing decisions that were dropped. Writes .orchestrator/memory/HOT.md with a first line stating it is generated by memory_hot and must not be edited, and marks the chosen records tier hot in the store (all others hot -> warm; cold unchanged). compact(root) = build and rewrite; idempotent. CLI: `orchestrator memory hot [--json]` (prints the view and the budget report), `orchestrator memory compact` (rebuilds HOT.md, prints pinned/dropped counts). Run migrate + compact against this repository's real memory files and report the token count and the pinned/dropped counts in the result and in docs/hermes-hardening/07-hot-memory.md. Do not touch spawn.py: packets are wired in the next task.
Repository rules: unittest (not pytest), tests/_harness.py single ORCH_ROOT fixture; every acceptance test id tests/test_<module>.py::test_name is a method def test_name(self) in a unittest.TestCase. No new third-party dependencies. Never write secret values to any file or log; test fixtures use synthetic names and values that are not credential-shaped. Do not quote template placeholder tokens (double braces) anywhere in code comments or docs. Shadow-first: a new adaptive path never changes what a worker sees until its mode is active; shadow only writes decision_log or runs rows. Run .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh . until green; the base suite must stay green. Do not ask questions: decide, and note decisions in the result summary. The interface contracts of the stage 1 modules are in .orchestrator/plan.md (section GOAL T-0991) and in docs/hermes-hardening/0*.md on this branch; read the merged module before building on it.
acceptance: tests/test_memory_hot.py::test_pinned_classes_never_dropped (unresolved gotcha, architecture, constraint decision and open-task records survive a tiny budget with over_budget true)
tests/test_memory_hot.py::test_budget_fill_by_score_and_tier_marks (higher-score records chosen first; store tiers updated; HOT.md written with the generated header)

risks.issue: Spec pins records whose source task is 'not merged/done/failed on the bus', but bus.STATUSES is only {queued,held,running,done,failed} — 'merged' isn't a real bus status (merge.py sets status='done' with merged_into set). Worse, real task files in this repo contain a 'superseded' status (40 of 1070 tasks) that the spec's closed-set never mentions, plus 2 tasks with a literal status='merged' written outside the formal STATUSES set. A closed-status denylist will misclassify superseded/off-schema tasks as 'open', permanently pinning their records and inflating over_budget.

build() needs 'all warm records' as candidates, but search() defaults to limit=20 and has no unbounded sentinel (limit=0 returns zero rows via 'LIMIT 0'). This repo currently has 257 warm records. If the executor calls search(None, tier='warm') without an explicit large limit, candidates silently truncate to 20 — the acceptance tests (small budgets, presumably few fixture records) won't catch this, but the spec's own required real-repo compact run will silently under-consider ~93% of warm records.

Kind-weight table in the spec (gotcha 3, decision 2, architecture 2, model_note 1, retrospective 1, strategy 1, skill_outcome 1) omits 'reference', one of the 8 kinds in KINDS. One reference record exists in real data today; its score weight is undefined.

Spec/pool.toml prose says pin decisions/records by 'source_task' (singular), matching the stale plan.md interface-contract wording, but the actual merged Record field is source_tasks (a list). Spec doesn't say whether pinning triggers on ANY or ALL open tasks in that list.

suggested_spec_changes: Replace the closed-status denylist with an open-status allowlist (queued/held/running, i.e. 'not observed as closed') or explicitly include superseded and any non-standard status alongside merged/done/failed, since production task files already drift outside bus.STATUSES.
Specify the exact warm-candidate fetch call, e.g. an explicit high limit (or a dedicated unbounded accessor) so 'all warm records' doesn't silently mean 'first 20 by rank/date'.
Define the score weight (or explicit exclusion) for kind='reference'.
Clarify pinning semantics for records with multiple source_tasks (any-open vs all-open) and correct 'source_task' wording to 'source_tasks' to match the merged schema.

State explicitly that hot_never_compact class labels ('gotcha:unresolved', 'decision:constraint') are conceptual buckets build() must special-case (kind+outcome / kind+tag heuristics), not literal Record.tags string matches — memory_store's markdown tagger never emits a literal 'constraint' tag today.

Note the tier-write mechanism explicitly: memory_store exposes no set_tier/bulk-update helper, so marking tiers means get() -> mutate -> add() per record (full row rewrite, sha recompute) for potentially all warm records on every compact() call.
